target-a.finding: target-a operates normally with vllm default max_num_seqs, no queueing, and p95 latency ~0.09 s through both direct and HAProxy paths.

target-b.finding: target-b is overloaded because max_num_seqs is set to 1, resulting in queue_waiting=4.0 and p95 latency ~4.5 s. error_rate is 0.0 but ok=false due to latency SLA breach.

payload.observations: Investigation complete. target-b has max_num_seqs=1 causing queue_waiting=4.0 and p95 latency ~4.5 s, while target-a uses vllm default with queue_waiting=0.0 and p95 latency ~0.09 s. Both have error_rate=0.0 and running container_state. The configuration diff (ev-002) and path-compare (ev-003) confirm the latency difference is due to the max_num_seqs mismatch. target-a is healthy; target-b is overloaded due to the single-slot limit.

moves.what_it_does: Stop routing new traffic to a worker. Mitigates a fault that software cannot repair (the path to the worker, or load it cannot carry); the cause still needs a human. Refused if no other worker is serving.

payload.expected_effect: New requests will no longer be routed to target-b. Existing in-flight requests may complete or be redirected to target-a, reducing queue_waiting from 4.0 to 0 and bringing p95 latency back to ~0.09 s fleet-wide.
payload.reasoning: target-b is overloaded due to max_num_seqs=1, causing queue_waiting=4.0 and p95 latency ~4.5 s. Draining target-b stops new requests from queuing on the single-slot worker, immediately improving user experience. target-a remains healthy and can serve all traffic during the drain. This move restores service for users while the root cause (configuration) is addressed separately.
payload.risk: Low. target-a is healthy and can absorb the traffic. Draining only affects target-b; no other workers are impacted. The underlying configuration mismatch (max_num_seqs=1) remains and will need a config change or restart to fully resolve, but the immediate user-visible fault is mitigated.
